units.name: count_text
units.signature: def count_text(text: str) -> tuple[int, int, int]
units.description: Return (lines, words, chars). lines = text.count('\n') plus 1 when text is non-empty and does not end with '\n'; words = len(text.split()); chars = len(text).

postconditions: returns (lines, words, chars), all non-negative ints
chars counts newline characters and Unicode characters, not bytes

units.name: main
units.signature: def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int
units.description: Parse argv (subcommand 'count' with one path). Read the file as bytes and decode as UTF-8 (no newline translation). Print 'lines words chars' to stdout and return 0. If the file does not exist, print nothing to stdout, write 'error: file not found: <path>' to stderr (stderr reconfigured to UTF-8 when possible) and return 2. The module calls sys.exit(main()) when run with -m.

preconditions: argv is a list of str or None (then sys.argv[1:] is used)
postconditions: returns 0 after printing exactly one line to stdout for an existing file
returns 2 with empty stdout and the exact error line on stderr when the file is missing

errors.condition: invalid command line (unknown subcommand or missing path): argparse exits with code 2

boundary_conditions: file without trailing newline counts its last line
path containing Korean characters in the error message
